result.summary: Require a dedicated, non-wildcard onion bind when automatic Tor onion service listening is enabled alongside explicit `-bind` arguments. Reject startup during initialization if explicit `-bind` parameters lack a specific `-bind=<addr>=onion` listener or specify a wildcard onion bind.
result.problem: When automatic onion service creation (`-listenonion`) runs without a dedicated onion bind, Tor forwards inbound traffic to the first normal P2P bind. Bitcoind cannot distinguish these from direct connections, misclassifying Tor peers by IP address and potentially granting them permissions assigned to the Tor daemon's local IP.
evidence: PR description: 'Tor peers arriving through shared or wildcard binds may be classified by IP and inherit address-based whitelist permissions.'
PR description cites consensus from #34892 recommending startup rejection rather than silent fallback.
result.scope_notes: This is a breaking startup configuration change: because `-listenonion` defaults to enabled whenever listening, existing node configs specifying `-bind` without Tor options will now fail startup until they add `-bind=<addr>=onion` or `-listenonion=0`.
result.changed_since_previous: Added release notes, tor documentation updates, and co-authors to commit messages.
result.card: PR 36170 causes bitcoind to refuse startup if automatic Tor listening is enabled alongside explicit -bind options without a dedicated, non-wildcard onion bind (-bind=<addr>=onion). Without a dedicated bind, incoming Tor connections land on standard listening sockets where they are misclassified by IP, potentially inheriting whitelist permissions assigned to the Tor daemon. Because -listenonion is enabled by default when listening, existing node setups using -bind will fail to start until they explicitly configure an onion bind or pass -listenonion=0.

risk.why: Nodes with existing configurations using explicit `-bind` directives will fail to start upon upgrading until their config files or startup arguments are modified.
